title: MCP servers
lead: MCP servers give chat more tools, such as searching documentation, drawing charts or reading your issue tracker. Add a server here, then turn it on in a chat’s Plugins. Chat uses it only when a request needs it.
empty: You haven’t added a server yet. Add one with the command that starts it or its URL, or paste the configuration from its instructions.
tryExample: To try one, add Microsoft Learn, which searches Microsoft’s documentation, such as Fabric’s and Power BI’s.

card.checkTitle: Start or connect to it, and list its tools
card.confirmRemove: Remove {{name}}? Chats that have it on stop using it.
card.noTools: It connected, and offers no tools.
card.needsSignIn: It needs you to sign in. The first time a message in a chat uses it, Fabricator opens its sign-in page in your browser.
card.exported: Exported to {{path}}. The file holds no keys.

form.pasteHint: Paste the JSON from the server’s instructions, its command or its URL. Fabricator fills in the form for you to check.
form.choose: It has {{total}} servers. Choose the one to add:
form.name: Name
form.commandHint: The command that starts the server, with its arguments, as you’d type it in a terminal. Fabricator runs it on this computer, in the app’s folder.
form.sse: It uses Server-Sent Events (SSE), as some older servers do

values.useProvider: Use a key from Model providers
values.useProviderLabel: Add a variable that gets a key you saved in Model providers
values.noProviders: To use a key you saved for a model provider instead of entering one, add it in Accounts → Model providers.

secrets.windows: For keys and tokens. Fabricator keeps their values in Windows Credential Manager, not in its settings, and never shows them again.
secrets.mac: For keys and tokens. Fabricator keeps their values in your Keychain, not in its settings, and never shows them again.

form.readOnlyHint: Chat can call only the tools the server marks as read-only, so it can’t change anything with the server. In a team app, that’s always the case.
form.trust: A server runs with your access to this computer and your accounts, and what chat sends it leaves Fabricator. Add only servers you trust.

parse.unreadable: That isn’t a configuration Fabricator can read. Paste the JSON from the server’s instructions.
parse.noServer: That configuration doesn’t have a server with a command or a URL.

tools.intro: Make your own tools: describe one, and Copilot writes it as an MCP server that runs on this computer, such as a tool that makes images with your OpenAI key.
tools.lead: Describe the tool, and Copilot writes it. Fabricator checks that it starts, then adds it to your MCP servers, so you can turn it on in a chat’s Plugins.

form.requestPlaceholder: Look up today’s exchange rates, and convert an amount from one currency to another.
form.requestHint: Say what it does, which service it uses and what it gives back. Copilot can read the service’s documentation as it works.
form.changePlaceholder: Let chat choose the image’s size: square, wide or tall.
form.keysHint: Keys it uses, such as an API key, as environment variables. Copilot sees their names, never their values, and you can add a value once it’s made.
form.trust: Copilot writes the tool, and Fabricator runs it on this computer with your access when chat uses it. Read its code under Code.

run.label: What Copilot did
run.failed: It didn’t start. Copilot is fixing it.
run.retrying: Copilot is starting again from what went wrong…
run.missingKeys_one: Its code reads {{keys}}, which it doesn’t get yet.
run.missingKeys_other: Its code reads {{keys}}, which it doesn’t get yet.
run.next: To use it, turn it on in a chat’s Plugins.
run.note: It usually takes a minute or two.
run.time: How long Copilot has worked on it
run.undone: {{name}} is back to how it was
run.onInChat: It’s on in this chat, which uses it as it is now from the next message.
run.closeAsk: Copilot is still working. Stop it and close?

code.label: The tool’s code
code.noDifference: The code is the same as before the change.
code.undoAsk: Undo the last change? {{name}} goes back to how it was before it, and the change is gone.

try.lead: Run one of its tools as chat would, with its keys, in a folder of its own that stands in for an app’s. A service it uses may charge you for it.
try.badJson: Enter the arguments as a JSON object.
try.reported: It reported a problem after {{seconds, number}} s.

import.lead: Someone shared this tool. Read what it does and its code before you add it: Fabricator runs it on this computer with your access when chat uses it.
import.asked: What it was made to do
import.keysHint: Enter your own keys: a shared tool never holds any.

errors.use: Couldn’t turn the tool on in this chat.

images.label: Make images
images.request: Make an image from a description with OpenAI’s latest image model, and save it as a PNG in the app’s public/images folder.

icons.label: Find icons
icons.request: Search Iconify’s free icon sets for icons that match a word, and save the one chat picks as an SVG in the app’s public/icons folder.

fonts.label: Add fonts
fonts.request: Download a font family from Google Fonts as WOFF2 files into the app’s public/fonts folder, and give back the @font-face CSS that uses them.

voice.label: Make voice-overs
voice.request: Turn text into speech with OpenAI’s text-to-speech API, and save it as an MP3 in the app’s public/audio folder.
